quotes.text: The biggest risk, of course, in the end of the day, are the people that used the tools. If they're not responsible, these are very powerful tools.

quotes.text: The agent is just simply something that's more focused. And by the way, you don't want to have an agent that does everything. An agent that can answer any kind of question. That's not the point of the agent.

quotes.text: If there's a one responsible policy on AI, is that you need to review your reports, those monitors every so often. And whenever you can, ask for insights.

quotes.text: Again, it pays that you've done what you should have done in the first place. Set up your security, set up your data policies, your data governance, the classifications and all that stuff.

chapters.title: Intro: Ralph Rivas, the Copilot Junkie
Autonomous agents and human in the loop
Pro code, low code and enterprise use cases

takeaways: Copilot only delivers value when data, security and governance are in order before it is switched on.
Use Copilot Studio for workflows inside one Microsoft 365 tenant and Microsoft Foundry when you need full control, multiple models or multi-tenant deployment.
Autonomous and proactive agents need a human in the loop and regular human review of their monitoring and reports.
hook: Copilot demos look impressive, but many organizations struggle to turn them into real business outcomes. Microsoft MVP Ralph Rivas explains what IT leaders, architects and makers must prepare in governance, security and agent design. You will learn when to use Copilot Studio versus Microsoft Foundry and how to keep autonomous agents under control.
